pr_title: [Bugfix] Validate lora adapters to avoid crashing server
pr_body:
This PR addresses an issue where loading an invalid lora adapter will crash the engine and shut the server down. This happens because dynamically loaded adapters are first loaded just-in-time, during model execution. Invalid adapters will raise at load time, and any exceptions raised during model execution will shut down the engine and the server.

Instead, this PR updates the `/v1/load_lora_adapter` handler to first call `engine.add_lora` to ensure that the adapter can be successfully loaded. On error, the adapter is not added to the list of available models to use. This should result in a better user experience, as users will immediately know if there is a problem with their adapter when they try to load it, instead of having it crash their server later when they try to use it.

FIX #11702

Ah, actually @jeejeelee this is a tiny bit more complex since both the initializer and `init_app_state` that call it are synchronous, so we can't easily `await self.engine_client.add_lora(lora_request)` here.

I can work around that, easiest option is to make `init_app_state` async, but the least disruptive option (in case some projects have made use of `init_app_state`) might be to load the static adapters on first request, and return an error to the user then if one doesn't load.

Let me know how that looks!
@joerunde Instead of try-catching `engine_client.add_lora` directly,  can we check for the different errors directly ? I believe it will be simpler. What do you think ?

I see. I am a bit concerned about the state changes that  LRUCacheWorkerLoRAManager::add_adapter does. Also given that the code was relying on the crash,  it may have not properly cleaned up. 

I was trying to see if we can implement a stripped down, static-method version of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e20c92bb618384ce8d0013e0c9ad273d0c23d65b/vllm/lora/worker_manager.py#L82 , so we can just try-catch on that.

Gotcha!

 > given that the code was relying on the crash, it may have not properly cleaned up
 
 I agree that's something to be aware of, but I think it's our responsibility to ensure that the underlying `_load_adapter` method and the state management bits in `add_adapter` are robust to failures. I don't think we can ever assume that `LRUCacheWorkerLoRAManager::add_adapter` will always be called with good and valid inputs, and since we need dynamic model registration then we're gonna have to deal with failures. It may not be robust today, but we can keep improving it. I can add some testing now to flex this a bit and see that load failures don't impact existing or future adapters.

> concerned about the state changes that LRUCacheWorkerLoRAManager::add_adapter does

Me too, it's not ideal that this can potentially evict another adapter. I think what I can do here is flip the logic in `add_adapter` around so it only evicts the oldest adapter after the new adapter successfully loads. That way you at least can't flood the server with bad adapter requests to force it to evict all the good adapters- the state only changes if the adapter is good.

I'm also slightly concerned about any race conditions with potentially evicting an adapter that's currently in use, but I think with all of our current v0 engine implementations the `add_adapter` call will happen in between model steps.


> I was trying to see if we can implement a stripped down, static-method version of...

Yeah we could try to call `_load_adapter` directly, but I think this gets hard in the multiprocessing case where the frontend process won't even have the class definition for the LoRA model to try to load :(. 
(And for the reasons in my last comment, I'd rather not try to duplicate the logic from `_load_model` in the frontend)

Yeah, I agree that we can land this and then make it better.

> I'm also slightly concerned about any race conditions with potentially evicting an adapter that's currently in use, but I think with all of our current v0 engine implementations the add_adapter call will happen in between model steps.

You are right, this should be fine. After the scheduler schedules all sequence for a `step`, we load all the requested LoRAs anyways. 

>  I think what I can do here is flip the logic in add_adapter around so it only evicts the oldest adapter after the new adapter successfully loads.
